exposure: maternal gut short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) levels (butyrate, isobutyrate, valerate, lactate)
maternal gut microbiota composition (Shannon diversity index of Firmicutes, Proteobacteria, and total microbiota)
outcome: cord blood (CB) Chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 17 (CCL17) serum levels
cohort: The study included healthy pregnant Japanese women (n=59 at 12 weeks of gestation, n=58 at 32 weeks of gestation).
finding: CB CCL17 levels correlated negatively with butyrate and positively with isobutyrate at 12 weeks, and positively with valerate and lactate at 32 weeks, while maternal non-specific IgE levels correlated negatively with butyrate and positively with lactate, suggesting maternal metabolites may alter fetal immune responses.
cross-section timing: Maternal stool samples were collected at 12 and 32 weeks of gestation; maternal serum at 32 weeks of gestation; cord blood serum at birth.
gest_age: Maternal samples collected at 12 and 32 weeks of gestation; cord blood collected at birth.
